properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously large breaking waves along the coast.

* WHERE...Northern Washington Coast zone.

* WHEN...Until noon PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous breaking waves can knock people off their
feet and sweep them into the ocean. Driftwood and debris in
powerful surf can injure or even kill people on the beach
observing the ocean. High surf will result in erosion to
beaches, dunes, and bluffs and may cause damage to roads,
trails, and coastal structures.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Significant log and debris pile-up on the
beaches and jetties from the high surf last weekend will pose
additional threats to those on the beaches and will exacerbate
coastal erosion.
properties.instruction:

surf zone. This includes staying off jetties, piers, and other
coastal structures. Never turn your back on the ocean and keep
children and pets close. Know the tides and forecast conditions.
Follow warning signs and respect barriers.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Moderate to heavy snowfall possible.

* WHERE...Anchorage and Eagle River (all elevations), East Turnagain
Arm, Western Kenai Peninsula, Southern Kenai Mtns, Interior Kenai
Peninsula, and Turnagain Pass.

* WHEN...From Saturday afternoon through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A snow band will set up and stall over
Anchorage/Kenai Peninsula tomorrow afternoon through Sunday
bringing rounds of moderate to heavy snowfall. There is moderate
uncertainty as to where the snow band will ultimately end up,
resulting in lower confidence for snowfall amounts. Warmer
temperatures filters in Sunday afternoon from east to west,
transitioning snow to rain.

*Low/High end values are as follows:

- Anchorage/Eagle River & western Kenai Peninsula: 2-4" (Low
end)/6-10" (High end). Higher elevations: up to a foot possible.

- Seward: 1-3" (Low end)/3-6" (High end).

- Turnagain Pass to Moose Pass: 7 to 11" possible.

- Portage: 9-11" with snowfall rates of up to 1" an hour.
properties.instruction: Monitor the latest forecasts for updates on this situation.

properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued November 14 at 2:00AM AST until November 14 at 5:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...This level of heat affects most individuals sensitive to
heat, especially those without effective cooling and/or adequate
hydration.

* WHERE...Portions of Puerto Rico and the u.S. Virgin Islands.

* WHEN...From 10 AM this morning to 5 PM AST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...High temperatures or elevated heat indices can worsen
symptoms in people with chronic conditions. They can also increase
the risk of heat-related illness among individuals sensitive to
heat with inadequate cooling or hydration. These risks are highest
across coastal areas, lowlands, interior valleys, and urban zones.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 13 at 9:19PM PST until November 15 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously large breaking waves 30 to 40 feet.

* WHERE...Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM PST Sunday. .

* IMPACTS...Breaking waves can sweep people off jetties and
docks, and into dangerous seas. Life-threatening surf
conditions and significant beach erosion can be expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...After only brief improvement late
Saturday through Sunday, a second large swell is forecast late
Sunday through Monday.
properties.instruction:
Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.

capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

dangerous surf conditions.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking
waves of 25 to 35 ft, with occasional sets of 40 to 50 ft at
favored breakpoints. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, large
breaking waves will run up beaches and crash over seawalls,
inundating adjacent, low-lying infrastructure.

* WHERE...All Pacific Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until 4 AM PST Sunday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, from midnight tonight to 6 PM PST
Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower
swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and
increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the
shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from
beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The Coastal Flood Advisory on Saturday is
specifically for the Pacific Coast, where large breaking waves
will spill over sea walls and run up beaches onto adjacent
infrastructure.
properties.instruction:

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other waterside
infrastructure.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

properties.areaDesc: Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 13 at 5:35PM PST until November 17 at 3:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to
8 feet Friday, increasing to 8 to 12 feet Saturday. Surf
heights are expected to decrease to 5 to 9 feet Sunday through
Tuesday. Dangerous rip currents expected. For the Coastal Flood
Advisory, minor to moderate coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches. Surf will
we highest for west-northwest facing beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 3 PM PST Tuesday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM to 4 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas that are normally dry,
especially around the time of high tide, including over beach
parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate to
significant beach erosion is likely. Isolated damage is
unlikely but possible. There is an increased risk for ocean
drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to
sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off
beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of significant west-
northwesterly swells are expected to produce large surf into
next week with highest surf and greatest impacts likely
peaking Saturday and potentially again Monday. Minor to
moderate coastal flooding impacts are possible, especially
when largest surf overlaps with peak high tides. Some of these
impacts may be moderate to significant beach erosion and
shallow flooding of normally dry beaches and walkways.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 13 at 5:35PM PST until November 14 at 6:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10
to 15 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the High Surf
Warning, dangerously large breaking waves of 18 to 25 feet
with dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Warning,
moderate to significant coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches. Surf will we highest
for west-northwest facing beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Friday. For
the High Surf Warning, from 9 PM Friday to 3 AM PST Sunday. For
the Coastal Flood Warning, from 3 AM to 6 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...There is a high risk for flooding of sea water over
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide. This includes significant flooding of coastal
beaches, walkways and roads, and potentially damaging some
structures. Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful
waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of
ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers and
jetties. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people
off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.
Remain far away from the water's edge.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of west-northwesterly swells
will create an extended period of large surf into next week,
with the potential for WARNING level surf again late Sunday
night through Monday. Areas that may see most significant
impacts will be west- northwest facing beaches, with
widespread flooding likely at low lying areas such as at
Oceano Dunes. Breaking waves may impact the Cayucos and Pismo
Beach piers as well as the Morro Bay Harbor entrance.
properties.instruction:
Stay off of beaches and coastal walkways, roads, and structures.
Do NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other water side
infrastructure.

* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 8
to 14 feet, peaking Saturday. Surf may locally reach 15 feet
near Ventura Harbor, where surf will likely be the largest.
Dangerous rip currents expected. For the Coastal Flood
Advisory, minor to moderate coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches. Surf will we highest
for west-northwest facing beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 3 PM PST Tuesday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM to 4 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas that are normally dry,
especially around the time of high tide, including over beach
parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate beach
erosion is likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible.
There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents
can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves
can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and
capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of significant west-
northwesterly swells are expected to produce large surf into
next week with highest surf and greatest impacts likely
peaking Saturday and potentially again Monday. Minor to
moderate coastal flooding impacts are possible, especially
when largest surf overlaps with peak high tides. Some of these
impacts may be moderate to significant beach erosion and
shallow flooding of normally dry beaches and walkways.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches
properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 13 at 5:35PM PST until November 15 at 3:00AM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10
to 15 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the High Surf
Warning, dangerously large breaking waves of 18 to 25 feet
with dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Warning,
moderate to significant coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches. Surf will we highest
for west-northwest facing beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Friday. For
the High Surf Warning, from 9 PM Friday to 3 AM PST Sunday. For
the Coastal Flood Warning, from 3 AM to 6 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...There is a high risk for flooding of sea water over
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide. This includes significant flooding of coastal
beaches, walkways and roads, and potentially damaging some
structures. Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful
waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of
ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers and
jetties. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people
off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.
Remain far away from the water's edge.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of west-northwesterly swells
will create an extended period of large surf into next week,
with the potential for WARNING level surf again late Sunday
night through Monday. Areas that may see most significant
impacts will be west- northwest facing beaches, with
widespread flooding likely at low lying areas such as at
Oceano Dunes. Breaking waves may impact the Cayucos and Pismo
Beach piers as well as the Morro Bay Harbor entrance.
properties.instruction:
Stay off of beaches and coastal walkways, roads, and structures.
Do NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other water side
infrastructure.

properties.areaDesc: Brevard, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 13 at 8:29PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Recent extreme rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River
has caused the river near Cocoa to rise to Major Flood Stage around
17.1 feet. Additional small rises are possible through the weekend
into next week, before river levels could begin to decline by late
next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:15 PM EST Friday the stage was 17.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:15 PM EST Friday was 17.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is forecast to rise to a crest of 17.2 feet
this weekend, hold steady around this level into next week, then
could begin to decline by late next week.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Saturday afternoon at noon EST.

properties.areaDesc: Harlan; Letcher
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 13 at 7:22PM EST by NWS Jackson KY
properties.description:
Multiple rounds of showers, mostly rain in the valleys and snow at
higher elevations, are expected tonight. Temperatures are cold enough
for minor snow accumulations at elevations above 2,500 feet, with
mainly a dusting to half inch on grassy and elevated surfaces.
However, localized 1 to 2 inch snow accumulations are possible over
the highest portions of Big Black Mountain. The snowfall combined
with air temperatures falling deep in the 20s could yield a few
slippery spots over the highest portions of Highway 160  near the
Kentucky-Virginia state line.
properties.instruction:
Monitor the weather situation closely and be alert for threatening
weather conditions.

NWSheadline: MINOR SNOW ACCUMULATIONS POSSIBLE ABOVE 2,500 FEET TONIGHT

properties.description:

from Saturday morning through Saturday night. Total snow
accumulations could range between 2 and 5 inches during this time.
Wind gusts to 35 mph could produce areas of blowing and drifting
snow. Travel may become difficult throughout this period.

NWSheadline: Blowing Snow with Moderate Accumulations Expected in the Eastern Brooks Range

properties.areaDesc: Ashe; Watauga; Tazewell; Smyth; Bland; Grayson; Mercer; Summers; Western Greenbrier
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 13 at 7:16PM EST by NWS Blacksburg VA
properties.description:
Snow showers will continue this evening through Saturday morning
from the mountains of southeast West Virginia into the High
Country of northwest North Carolina.

Accumulations will be light for most, ranging from a coating to
locally near an inch for most, and perhaps slightly more for
elevations above 3,000 feet. These snow showers will also produce
brief and localized reductions in visibility.

Slick roads and difficult driving conditions are possible tonight
and Saturday morning. Please allow extra time to reach your
destination.

NWSheadline: ......ACCUMULATING SNOW EXPECTED TONIGHT......

properties.areaDesc: Clatsop County Coast; Tillamook County Coast; South Washington Coast
properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 13 at 4:07PM PST until November 14 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Portland OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Large waves and dangerous surf conditions. Breakers 30 to
35 feet.

* WHERE...Clatsop and Tillamook Coast, and South Washington
Coast.

* WHEN...Until noon PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties,
and other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off
rocks and jetties and drown while observing high surf. Severe
beach erosion may destroy coastal properties and buildings.
Higher than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low-
lying shoreline.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme
during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people
off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean
which may lead to serious injury or drowning. The sneaker wave
threat will peak Friday evening into Friday night.
properties.instruction:
A High Surf Warning means that high surf will affect beaches,
producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the
beach can lift or roll logs which can injure or kill someone
caught in their path.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 13 at 6:55PM EST by NWS Charleston WV
properties.description:
Snow showers will continue tonight into Saturday morning across
the mountains of West Virginia and southwest Virginia.

Accumulations will be light for most with a coating to an inch
expected below or around elevations of 2,500 feet. Elevations
above 2,500 feet however could see accumulations between 1-3" with
bands of moderate to heavy snow showers through Saturday morning.

Slick and snow covered roads are possible tonight and Saturday
morning. Please allow extra time to reach your destination and
remain aware of hazardous road conditions.

NWSheadline: ......ACCUMULATING SNOW EXPECTED TONIGHT......

properties.areaDesc: Cook, IL; Lake, IN
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued November 13 at 5:31PM CST until November 14 at 9:00AM CST by NWS Chicago IL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Extreme Southeast Central Cook County in northeastern
Illinois...
Central Lake IN County in northwestern Indiana...

* WHEN...Until 900 AM CST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding
may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Storm drains and
ditches may be clogged with leaf debris increasing the risk of
flooding.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 530 PM CST, Doppler radar indicated lake effect rain. Minor
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the advisory
area. Several creeks and streams are rising, including the Turkey
Creek near Merrillville which has recently risen above bankfull.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Chicago, Hammond, Gary, Calumet City, Merrillville, South Shore,
East Chicago, Schererville, Hobart, Lansing, Crown Point,
Highland, Munster, Cedar Lake, Griffith, Dyer, South Deering, St.
John, Lake Station, Lynwood, Lakes of the Four Seasons, Whiting,
Winfield and New Chicago.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
A Flood Advisory means minor flooding along waterways and other poor
drainage areas is imminent or may already be occurring. Persons in
the advisory area should use caution and avoid flood waters.

properties.headline: Marine Weather Statement issued November 13 at 2:53PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
A large west to northwesterly swell is expected to produce
breaking waves at the Morro Bay and Ventura Harbor entrances
on Saturday. These conditions have a history of capsizing vessels
of various sizes resulting in serious injury or death, even to
the most experienced mariners. Mariners are urged to stay clear of
these harbor entrances. For more information, contact the local
harbor patrol or coast guard station...and continue to monitor
NOAA Weather Radio for the latest weather information..

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of northwest Washington, including the following
county, Mason.

* WHEN...Through late Saturday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Three to four inches of rain is forecast for the south slopes of
the Olympics through early Sunday with snow levels of 5500 to
6500 feet. The combination of heavy rain and relatively high snow
levels could push the Skokomish River near Potlatch above flood
stage.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 13 at 12:01PM PST until November 14 at 10:00AM PST by NWS Sacramento CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow is expected for elevations above 6000 feet. Total snow
accumulations 6 to 12 inches, with up to 18 inches at the highest
peaks. Minor accumulations of around an 2 inch possible down to
5000 feet. Winds could gust as high as 60 mph.

* WHERE...Northern Sierra above 6000 feet, including Highway 50,
Interstate 80, State Route 4, State Route 108, Southern Cascades
above 6000 feet, including Lassen National Park.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions
will impact the Friday evening commute. Strong winds could cause
downed tree branches, localized power outages, and reduced
visibilities.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow levels 6500 to 7500 feet Today, dropping
to 5500 to 6000 feet Saturday morning. Heaviest snowfall expected
this afternoon through the overnight hours. Snowfall rates of 1 to
2 inches per hour, with locally up to 3 inches per hour in
convective bands. Light flurries to 2 inches possible down to 5000
feet with higher accumulations remaining above 6000 feet. Lull in
activity Saturday afternoon through Sunday, followed by additional
snow Sunday night through Monday.
properties.instruction:

quickmap.dot.ca.gov or dial 5 1 1.

expected. Minor tidal flooding often results in some road
closures. Usually, the most vulnerable roadways will flood.

Do not leave your vehicle at a location that is prone to tidal
flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The
water may be deeper than you think it is. You will be putting
yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to
costly repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous, large breaking waves of 20 to 25 ft this
morning, increasing to a peak of 30 to 35 ft late this
afternoon through Saturday morning. Another round of dangerous
surf conditions is expected Sunday night, with breaking waves
reaching 25 to 30 ft and persisting into Monday morning. Waves
gradually diminish through Monday evening, but remain
hazardous through the day.

* WHERE...Beaches of South Central Oregon Coast and Curry County
Coast. This includes Charleston, Port Orford, Gold Beach, and
Brookings.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM PST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Extremely large breaking waves will create very
hazardous conditions along beaches and area shorelines. Waves
will inundate beaches and surge into normally dry areas.
Infrastructure damage and significant beach erosion can be
expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Breaking waves will briefly ease Saturday
night to 15 to 20 ft, but quickly rise to dangerous heights
again Sunday afternoon and evening.
properties.instruction:

and life-threatening surf conditions. Stay off of beaches, rocks,
jetties,piers, and other waterside infrastructure.

properties.areaDesc: Greater Lake Tahoe Area; Greater Lake Tahoe Area
properties.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 13 at 1:32AM PST until November 14 at 10:00AM PST by NWS Reno NV
properties.description:
* CHANGES...None.

* WHAT...Heavy wet snow. Snow accumulations near 12 inches above 7000
feet, with up to 6 inches below 7000 feet. Snow accumulations up to
20 inches along the crest west of Lake Tahoe. Wind gusts of 70 to
90 mph over ridges and gusts of 45 to 55 mph for Truckee and Lake
Tahoe communities. Wave heights 2 to 5 feet on Lake Tahoe.

* WHERE...Greater Lake Tahoe Area.

* WHEN...From 10 AM this morning to 10 AM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions
could impact the Friday evening commute. Strong winds and Sierra
cement snow could cause damage to trees and power lines. Strong
winds and rough waves on Lake Tahoe will create hazardous
conditions for small watercraft.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A burst of heavy snow is likely with this
system late this afternoon into the evening with snow levels
falling to as low as 5500 feet.
properties.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, and water in your
vehicle in case of an emergency. The latest road conditions for the
state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 12 at 8:10PM EST by NWS Jackson KY
properties.description:
Multiple rounds of showers, mostly rain in the valleys and snow at
higher elevations, are expected on Friday and Friday night.
Temperatures should be cold enough for minor snow accumulations at
elevations above 2,500 feet with mainly a dusting to half inch on
grassy and elevated surfaces. However, localized 1 to 2 inch snow
accumulations are possible over the highest portions of Big Black
Mountain. The snowfall combined with air temperatures falling deep in
the 20s could yield a few slippery spots over the highest portions of
Highway 160  near the Kentucky-Virginia state line, especially on
Friday night.
properties.instruction:
Monitor the weather situation closely and be alert for threatening
weather conditions.
